posts.body:
I have almost finished storyboarding for an RPG which spans the present, past and future.
(I don't intend to work on it until I've made a couple smaller games, first, but I've storyboards and planned it for a long time).
What considerations or constraints make the decision for RPGMaker MZ as to whether it should be released as one game or in installments (a 2, 3 or 4 parter).
I feel I can't answer that question for myself as I don't know the limitations of MZ in terms of scalability.
But I do need to answer it, as it will change the direction I take some of the build up scenes, and of course  the naming of things .
I've got it down to one...
tilesets
is it realistic to capture three separate timezone tilesets in one project?

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Among indie games, episodic releases has become pretty popular...though admitedly that tends to be with horror games.
So, I think people can be tolerant of it, but I'm personally not a fan.
The thing is, you are a new developer without a track record of delivering on products, so I think many people would be hesitant to buy an episode until you've proven you can release all the episodes.
Game development is hard, so as a result many people either give up, or spend way, way longer developing their game than they plan.
And it's really hard to keep up that development momentum when you release the first episode, see either no one downloads it or no one likes it, but you have now obligated yourself to finishing the next 4 or 5 or however many episodes. Or you can risk your reputation and give up and never release those episodes.
The other consideration is that it winds up becoming management of multiple games. If each episode is a standalone part, that means you'll need to manage patching the previous episodes while also developing the next episode. Might be fine when you have episode 1 released and developing the next, but the more episodes you release, the bigger that backlog of past episodes gets that you'll have to maintain.
Unless you are confident in your abilities to polish the game with what will likely be limited feedback, you're going to end up having a huge backlog of games to patch.
There is also a technical consideration here as it's not easy to transfer data from one RPG Maker game into another. It's not impossible, but likely might require a custom plugin. So either you'd be spending money on a custom plugin (unless you're capable of programming it yourself) or you would need to ensure that each episode is it's own standalone part of the story. But then, why sell it as "episodic" at that point?
As a new developer, I would focus on a smaller game first, and I would avoid episodic releases unless you have high confidence in your abilities as a developer and a clear and well structured plan on development and release structure of future episodes.
Good luck.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: Personally I think it's fine as long as each episode can stand alone as a story and has "enough" content to be equivalent to a full game. Otherwise the player might feel ripped off.
